$comment: Shared state for ONE work-graph run. Lives at .graph/runs/<run-id>/state.json. Every node reads this on start and appends to its OWN key on finish - the builder writes its own builders.<slice> key, including the branch it worked on. Never rewrite another node's key. Every node key carries written_by, naming the node that wrote it: that is the ONLY record of authorship this file has, and without it 'never rewrite another node's key' is unverifiable - an orchestrator hand-writing all six keys is indistinguishable from six nodes doing their jobs. verify-state.py --audit checks it. This file is the edge: it is how context crosses between agents that cannot see each other.

architect.rationale: Single-loop, one builder, one branch off orchestra main @ 3422e61, slices run in order s1 -> s2 -> s3 -> s4. A diamond is not earned here. (1) Every slice uses s1's artifact (protocol/fixtures + the TS codec), so s1 has to come first and only s2/s3/s4 could run in parallel. s3 and s4 are each about one file, so the fan-out buys almost no time. (2) The likeliest failure is the Rust copy finding that serde cannot express a shape the TS fixtures pinned (adjacent method/args tagging under deny_unknown_fields, flatten). The fix then lands back in protocol/fixtures, which is s1's file set. That is exactly the overlap that breaks a fan-in. (3) It is one app and one reviewable diff, and the TS and Rust copies are best written by the one builder who wrote the fixtures. Risk tags: s1 high: it is the source of truth that every other slice consumes, and its tolerance rules (unknown enum to plain text, unknown event ignored) are logic a round-trip test passes whether or not they are lenient in the right places. s2 high: it touches desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs (shell file) and moves the deny_unknown_fields IPC arg structs, which are the host's input-validation boundary. A dropped deny_unknown_fields still compiles and still passes the happy-path tests. s3 low: no sensitive data, no file another slice touches, metro.config.js is not in the native high-risk list (app.json/app.config/eas.json), no native module or config plugin, so no runtimeVersion change (no build exists yet either). The one thing tests cannot see (Metro actually bundling ../protocol) is covered by a recorded scratch-import step in done_when. s4 low: wording only, in two docs no other slice touches, no data.
decisions_for_gate: G1 ack: dropped. README.md:130-159 is the record and has no ack. result{id} is the acknowledgement of a call. ROADMAP.md:286 is stale and gets fixed locally (gitignored).

G2 notice: not typed in v1 code. The event name 'notice' is reserved in the constants (README:155), but no payload type exists until H2 (README:196). Adding an event does not bump v (README:178), and clients ignore unknown event names (G6), so H2 adds it with no v2. core/notify.rs is untouched.

G3 frame size: MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES = 4194304 (4 MiB) for one decoded JSON message, UTF-8 bytes, checked first by both decoders (oversize -> bad_request). Why not smaller: snapshot carries every InboxItem, and one item can hold several 32 KiB text fields. Splitting a message into Noise messages (65535 bytes max each) is P3's job. MAX_TEXT_BYTES stays 32768. Alternative for the gate: 1 MiB.

G4 field types and closed sets: v is the integer 1. type is a string. call.id is a non-empty string of at most 128 bytes. seq is a non-negative integer (u64 / safe JS integer), and the codec does not check its ordering (P3). welcome.scopes is an array drawn from read|answer|control|land. welcome.features is an array of strings, empty in v1 (push is reserved, not sent). host_id and host_name are strings. hello.client_name and hello.app_version are strings. Every client-sent string is capped at MAX_TEXT_BYTES. result has exactly one of ok (any JSON; null for unit commands) or error{code,message}. Handshake frames are {proto:orchestra, v} and {proto, v, supported:[1]}, with no type field; they get their own decode functions. The method set is the 15 names at README:143-146; pick_project is not a wire method (-> bad_request). Method->scope is the README:86-91 table as data. It is not enforced in P2.

G5 snapshot payloads: full types, per the mirror rule (README:161). projects: Project[] {id,name}. sessions: SessionSummary[]. inbox: the full InboxItem[], the same as list_inbox. tasks: TaskSummary[]. storage: StorageStatus. No summary type.

G6 client tolerance (README:179-180), host input strict (README:181). The client decoder keeps unknown enum string values verbatim as plain text: session/task status, inbox kind, model, permission_mode, scope, feature, error code, diff file status. It ignores unknown fields. An unknown event name decodes to an unknown-event value, not an error. Optional agent?: string and host?: string are declared on the wire SessionSummary/TaskSummary (host? also on InboxItem). They are absent from core output today, and core types are not changed for D7/D8. pr (D6) is not declared, because its shape (checks) is undecided. An unknown v, in either direction, is a loud error (unsupported_version). An unknown type at a known v is unknown_type. Host decode of client messages is deny_unknown_fields everywhere, including hello and the handshake frame.

G7 error codes, closed set on the host: unsupported_version, unknown_type, bad_request, forbidden, revoked, already_answered, failed. Two are new beyond the README: bad_request (malformed JSON, wrong field type, unknown field, oversize, unknown method, string over its cap) and failed (a command's String error, mapped in P3). error may carry supported:[1] (README:136). The client side keeps an unknown code as plain text (G6).

Structural S1: the Rust module is orchestra_core::wire (core/src/wire/), not protocol, to avoid core/src/session/protocol.rs. The arg structs (StartArgs, CreateTaskArgs, CancelTaskArgs, TaskIdArgs, StopArgs, TranscriptArgs, Answer) move from desktop/src-tauri/src/commands.rs to core/src/wire/args.rs with deny_unknown_fields unchanged. commands.rs then imports them. One Rust copy, not two. Core gains Deserialize on its host-output payload types (no deny_unknown_fields there) so h2c fixtures can round-trip. No new crates.

Structural S2: consumption with no workspace. Relative imports only, no path alias, no copy step, no package.json in protocol/. protocol/ uses extensionless relative imports and erasable TS only (no enum or namespace, import type), so desktop tsc, mobile tsc, Vite, Metro and Babel all compile it as source. Mobile: Metro needs watchFolders, because Expo getWatchFolders returns [] outside a workspace and Metro will not resolve a file outside its watched roots. So mobile/metro.config.js = getDefaultConfig(__dirname) + watchFolders [../protocol]. jest-expo needs no config: imports outside rootDir resolve and transform, and the test file sits under mobile/src so the default roots discover it. Desktop: no runtime import in P2. Vite dev server.fs.allow would block ../protocol. H3 puts the client socket in Rust, so the webview may never need it. Desktop only runs the canonical TS fixture test (vitest, desktop/src/protocol.test.ts). That test also type-asserts that desktop/src/types.ts payload types are assignable to the wire types and that desktop MAX_TEXT_BYTES equals the protocol constant, so the TS copies are locked without rewiring the desktop.

Wording, protocol/README.md (s1 touches it anyway): (a) :5-6 'It holds no code and no schema files' becomes a pointer to the code and fixtures. (b) A short 'P2 decided' paragraph under 'What P2 and P3 decide' records G3, G4 and G7 once approved. (c) The three P1 review notes: :199 'D6, D7 or D8 changing shape reopens the matching item' is replaced by the stock 'no reversal condition was recorded at the gate' line; :30-31 SSH tunnel 'Rejected' gains 'for v1'; :193 host_id in welcome is reworded as applying regardless of D8. The gate may veto (c) item by item.
architect.fixture_contract: One case per file in orchestra/protocol/fixtures/*.json, plus constants.json. A case is {name, dir: c2h|h2c|hs_c2h|hs_h2c, wire: JSON value, or raw: string for malformed JSON, expect: ok | {error: code}, client_only?: true}. For ok: decode(stringify(wire)) succeeds, and encode(decoded) deep-equals wire (key order ignored), in both copies. For an error: decode fails with exactly that code in both copies. client_only cases (unknown enum values, extra fields, unknown event name) get the full check in TS only; Rust checks only that they parse as JSON. constants.json = {v, supported, max_text_bytes, max_message_bytes, methods, method_scope, event_names (incl. reserved notice), scopes, error_codes}. Both copies assert that their constants equal it. Rust reads the directory at test time via CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR/../protocol/fixtures (read_dir, so there is no list to drift). TS imports through protocol/fixtures/index.ts, and the desktop test asserts with import.meta.glob that index.ts covers every *.json. The oversize case is generated in code in both runners, not checked in. Minimum coverage: every message type in both directions, all 15 methods with valid args, all 3 answer kinds, both handshake replies, unsupported v both directions, missing v, unknown type, unknown field on c2h (bad_request), pick_project (bad_request), unknown status/agent/host/event name (client_only ok).

s1.summary: PASS. Re-ran all six done_when on the branch tip in C:/Users/natha/wt/op2: protocol tsc exit 0, protocol.test.ts 95/95, npm test 153/153, npm run build exit 0, README grep 0, no desktop package diff. I probed the decoders with about 60 inputs the fixtures do not cover: v 1.0, "1", null, -1 and 1.5; a missing or null type; null fields; negative, fractional and 2^60 seq; a 64-char/128-byte non-ASCII id (accepted) and 65 chars (rejected); 11000 x U+20AC and 8193 emoji prompts (rejected); __proto__ keys; result with both or neither of ok/error; unknown scope, code, event and pong extras. Every result matched G4/G6/G7, and v is checked before type and fields. ProtocolError works with instanceof, code, message, name and String(). I ran 22 mutations in a scratch copy and the tests caught 20. Two survived and are notes: the call.id cap counting chars instead of bytes, and moving the v check after the field checks. README edits match G3/G4/G7 and wording items a-c. All files are in plan, and the commits are njcurtis3 with no attribution. Worktree left clean.

findings.issue: No fixture locks the v-first check order. In a scratch copy I moved the unsupported_version check after the type, field and proto checks in all four decoders, and all 95 tests still passed. The realistic v2 message ({v:2,type:'subscribe'} or {v:2,type:'call',...,new_field}) could therefore come back as unknown_type or bad_request in either copy, and nothing would catch it. The code is correct today (envelope() in codec.ts and codec.rs). Add c2h/h2c/hs fixtures with v:2 plus an unknown type or unknown field, expecting unsupported_version.

The call.id 128-byte cap is checked only with ASCII ids (c2h.err_id_too_long, c2h.ok_id_max). Changing utf8Length(id) to id.length at codec.ts:284 survived all tests. The code is correct (65 x U+00E9 = 130 bytes is rejected), but the byte rule is not locked for either copy. Add a non-ASCII id fixture of 65 x U+00E9, expecting bad_request.

utf8Length reads a high surrogate followed by a non-low-surrogate as one 4-byte pair. A JSON-escaped prompt of 8192 x '�一' counts as 32768 and is accepted by decodeClientMessage, although it is 49152 bytes as UTF-8 with replacement. serde_json rejects lone surrogates, so the Rust host returns bad_request: the two copies disagree. This is low impact, because the TS strict decoder is not the host in v1. Fix: count 4 only when the next unit is 0xDC00-0xDFFF, or reject lone surrogates.

answer{kind:question} with answers {"__proto__":"x","q":"y"} decodes to answers {q:'y'}. The out[k]= assignment on a {} literal hits the __proto__ setter, which ignores a string, so the key is dropped silently, where Rust keeps it as a map key. Low impact for the same reason as the surrogate note. Fix: Object.create(null) or Object.defineProperty.

{v:1.0} (and 1e0) is accepted by the TS decoders, because JSON.parse cannot tell it from 1. core/src/wire/codec.rs integer() presumably returns bad_request for it. This is a cross-copy divergence with no fixture, though no conforming encoder emits 1.0. Leave it or pin it with a fixture. Not a v1 behaviour risk.

An unknown transcript entry kind fails the whole transcript-appended event or get_transcript decode with bad_request on the client. This matches G6, whose open-enum list leaves out entry kind, but it means a new entry kind is in effect a v bump for clients. A future reader of README 'Versioning' may expect that to be tolerant. Record it, or make an unknown kind a passthrough record, when entry kinds next change.

The ProtocolError stack's first line reads 'Error: <msg>', not 'ProtocolError: <msg>', because the stack is borrowed from new Error(). Cosmetic only: instanceof ProtocolError/Error, .code, .message, .name and String(e) are all correct.

findings.issue: Client-side decode_host reads event seq with Value::as_u64, so seq 1.0 is bad_request in Rust and ok in TS (Number.isSafeInteger). Rust also accepts seq above 2^53, which TS rejects. Hosts emit integers, so nothing triggers it today. No fixture covers it; worth one when P3 adds a Rust client.
An unknown event with no payload key decodes to payload Null and re-encodes as payload: null. TS leaves it undefined and omits the key. Client-side only, no fixture.

assert_eq!(ran, files.len()) is tautological: ran is incremented once per file, client_only skips included. The real anti-drift guards are read_dir (no list) and the ran >= 80 floor, and both are sound. The done_when wording is met, but the equality catches nothing.
serde_json rejects a lone UTF-16 surrogate escape as not JSON (bad_request), while JSON.parse accepts it. Rust is stricter than TS on host input, which is the safe direction.
